skill.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skill.description: Coordinate multiple AI subagents on independent coding problems, then review and integrate their findings safely.
skill.summary: Parallelize independent coding investigations with focused agent tasks and a structured integration review.
skill.author: CodingCossack

content.value_statement: Large coding investigations slow down when unrelated failures are handled one at a time. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code split independent work into focused subagent tasks and integrate results.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when failures are independent enough for parallel agent work.
Provides a checklist for scoping, dispatching, reviewing, and integrating subagent results.
Shows how to write focused agent tasks with scope, goals, constraints, and output expectations.
Includes examples for splitting failing tests across separate files or subsystems.
Defines review steps for checking file conflicts and rerunning the full test suite.
limitations: Does not provide an executable orchestration tool or automation script.
Assumes the user has access to an agent system that can run parallel tasks.
Requires human review before integrating changes from multiple agents.
Is not suitable for failures that share state, files, or ordering dependencies.

use_cases.title: Split Failing Test Suites
use_cases.description: A developer can assign separate test files to different agents when the failures do not share code paths.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Refactor Follow-Up
use_cases.description: A tech lead can divide independent regressions after a large refactor and review each agent's summary.

use_cases.title: Triage Independent Bugs
use_cases.description: A maintainer can turn unrelated bug reports into scoped tasks with clear constraints and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Find Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failures and group them by independent files or subsystems. Mark anything that should stay in a single investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Create Agent Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one focused agent task for each independent domain. Include scope, goal, constraints, and required summary format.

prompt_templates.title: Review Agent Outputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these agent summaries for file conflicts, shared assumptions, and missing test coverage before I integrate the fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Parallel Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a complete parallel-agent workflow for these failures. Include domain grouping, dispatch prompts, integration checks, and rerun criteria.

output_examples.input: Six failures are split across three unrelated test files after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends three separate agent tasks, one per test file, followed by conflict review and a full test suite rerun.

output_examples.input: Two failing tests touch the same shared state manager.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends investigating them together first, because one fix may affect both failures.

output_examples.input: An agent returns a fix summary after changing one scoped file.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends checking whether any other agent edited the same file before merging the result.

best_practices: Parallelize only when each agent owns a clearly separate file, subsystem, or failure domain.
Give every agent a narrow scope, a concrete goal, explicit constraints, and an expected summary.
Review all summaries and rerun the full test suite before accepting the combined result.
anti_patterns: Do not send vague requests like fixing all tests to a single agent batch.
Do not parallelize failures that may share state, timing, or code ownership.
Do not merge multiple agent changes without checking for file conflicts and new failures.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you have two or more independent coding problems that can be investigated without shared state or ordering dependencies.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and prompt patterns for tools that already support subagents or parallel task dispatch.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples are written for Claude Code Task-style dispatch, and the workflow also fits Claude and Codex planning.

faq.question: How do I know work is independent?
faq.answer: Work is independent when each task can be fixed without changing the same files, shared state, or dependent execution order.

faq.question: What should each agent return?
faq.answer: Each agent should return the root cause, the files changed, the fix applied, and any tests run or still needed.

faq.question: What is the main review step?
faq.answer: Check whether agents edited overlapping files, read their summaries, resolve conflicts, and rerun the full test suite.
